correctness.rationale: The greedy arch length budget is exactly two, forcing a unique 001 arch plus a final 1 and no other surplus configuration under Dyck height nonnegativity. All permitted two-letter arches before/after it are classified exhaustively. The full SAS count is calculated by six explicit pair-absence matrices and the established shortest-absent gluing lemma, with positivity and n=2,3 boundary cases checked. The Fibonacci ordered-coordinate induction proves the upper bound and uniquely identifies the equality choices. An independent next-occurrence dynamic program exhaustively corroborates all Dyck paths of semilength <=12; direct SAS word tests and longer witnesses are supplementary and do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The condition is naturally the one-unit defect below the length-imposed upper bound for subsequence universality of balanced Dyck words, rather than an arbitrary finite or normalization slice. It has a nontrivial Catalan-height obstruction that forces one exceptional arch and yields an exact 2^{n-1}-1 structural subclass plus a sharp F_n SAS maximum and complete one/two-extremizer classification. These quantify a natural tradeoff between near-complete scattered-pattern coverage and missing-pattern ambiguity, strictly sharpening unrestricted Fibonacci bounds.
